subject: ANALYSIS lowering-opus: app-switcher blur cost, device-calibrated from c6o xnu-live.log; the 107..155 'jobs' are Dispatches, not kernel jobs; plan
body: 1) Counts: TEGU_COMMAND_FAILED jobs=107..155 counts Dispatches (draws+clears). Real kernel submissions = NORD2 GPU JOBS n (= TEGU_PERF_BATCH jobs, e.g. window @11938: 684 kernel jobs / 48 cmds = 14/cmd; PERF_FRAME kernel_jobs=2437 there counts something else). App-switcher windows @11553-11719: 27-38 kernel jobs/cmd (fs 15-20, offscreen 12-18), 15-24 passes/cmd, exec 38-48 ms/cmd. 2) Per kernel job on device: q 52 us (incl. clean ~45), inv ~38, gap ~85 => ~0.17-0.2 ms kernel fixed; GPU run avg 0.44-0.6 ms (max 3-6 ms). Sum of kernel job lifetimes is only ~40% of the frontend's gpu_ms (e.g. 684x0.52=358 ms vs gpu_ms 944 in the same 2 s): ~0.8 ms per kernel job is USERLAND between submissions (bridge/n2r build, MIG submit+wait, async reaping). So the 'fixed ~0.5 ms per job' is real but mostly userland, and it applies to ~30 jobs/cmd, not 107-155: ~9-15 ms of the 38-48 ms. 3) Estimate for the app-switcher blur frame (after today's correctness fix, blur pyramids render again): add ~10-16 tiny pyramid/blur passes ~ +8-13 ms => ~45-60 ms/cmd today. With one submission per command (all passes chained: JS1 tiler chain of every frame + JS0 fragment chain, one cache-maintenance round, one wait) saving ~0.3-0.5 ms per merged job: -10 to -18 ms. Pass-MRT on (NORD2_METAL_PASS_MRT=1, removes the 2-attachment in-pass splits + memfetch of fixed_frag inputs, ~1.2 ms per fullscreen job removed): -8 to -15 ms. Both: ~22-30 ms/cmd (~35-45 fps) for this frame; 60 fps also needs fewer fullscreen passes/GPU time (fs jobs ~2 ms each). Range wide: no per-job histogram in the log. 4) ansuz (references/ansuz-metal) does NOT chain passes either: one vertex+fragment chain PER PASS, one shared tiler heap, kernel serialisation; its blur passes cost 1.2-2.6 ms GPU; their 'one SUBMIT per group / chain of fragment jobs' is listed as a NEXT item (NATIVE-METAL 18.4); their per-call saving came from IOConnectTrap (kernel round trip 20-25 us MIG -> ~1.6 us trap) = our #12 trap item (kernel side pending). 5) Plan (bridge, mine): n2mb chained submission of K consecutive frames, default OFF (NORD2_METAL_CHAIN=1): tiler chains concatenated (indices/deps continue), fragment jobs linked with barrier+dependency, each frame's tiler context on its own heap slice (no shared-heap reset hazard), <=32 handles per submission, pooled blocks retired by the one job id; host tests on chain structure. Hazards needing a device A/B before default-on: texture-cache coherence between fragment jobs inside one chain (frame k+1 samples frame k), heap slice sizing. Kernel side (KA): job_finish cleans/invalidates EVERY GPU-writable BO of the context per job (inv ~600 KiB/job); restricting to the job's write-listed BOs and the trap path are the cheapest kernel wins. Not done: per-pass merge of pyramid levels (each level samples the previous one: needs completion, i.e. the chain); skipping intermediates' store is not exact (next level samples them).
